Good afternoon, passengers on flight twenty-two fourteen to Chicago. This flight is overbooked, and we are looking for three volunteers to take a later flight. If you volunteer, we will rebook you on the eight p.m. flight, and you will receive a travel voucher for four hundred dollars and a meal voucher. Passengers with a short layover, please do not leave the gate area. If you are interested, please come to the desk with your boarding pass. We also ask all passengers to have their passports ready. Thank you.

I travel for work about eighty days a year, and I have missed many connecting flights. Here is what I have learned. First, never book a layover shorter than two hours, especially on international trips. Second, when your flight is cancelled, call the airline while you wait in line at the desk. The first person who answers will rebook you. Third, always ask about compensation. Last year, an agent told me that the airline could not help. I asked her politely if she could check again, and in the end she gave me a hotel room and a voucher. And finally, keep your medicine and one clean shirt in your carry-on bag, because baggage claim is not always a happy place.
